have alternatives; I can go to the cinema if I like, or for a walk, but studying

We use “still“ for something that is in progress at the moment, whereas
we use “yet“ for something that has not begun or happened.

“yet” in questions and negative sentences, but not always. We must learn

We use the 3rd conditional to communicate that we are imagining
something in the past that did not really happen. Its construction is “If“
+ past perfect + “would have done“. The sentence “If I had gone to the
park yesterday, I would have played football“ means that, in fact, I did not
go to the park yesterday, and I did not play football; I am only imagining.
